articleTitle: The electricity distribution system-a national asset
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Future for Research in Transmission and Distribution in the UK
abstract: A number of regional electricity companies (RECs) are beginning to develop a corporate R&D policy. One of the most important developing areas is helping to reduce the costs of distributing electricity. The author looks at the need for R&D in distribution engineering and how it can be funded.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Regulation and research and development (electricity supply industry)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Future for Research in Transmission and Distribution in the UK
abstract: The Electricity Act 1989 lays down the duties of the Director General of Electricity Supply and of the Secretary of State in relation to all aspects of the privatised electricity supply industry including research and development. The author looks at the regulatory influence and implementation of duties of these two key people.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Future for Research in Transmission and Distribution in the UK
abstract: Privatisation of the electricity supply industry in the UK has brought radical influences to bear on the transmission network. The industry is under pressure to improve performance efficiency with respect to customers while maintaining competitive tariffs and also to generate high profit margins to provide dividends to shareholders and funds for investment in the business. There is therefore a need to continue research and development and collaboration between regional electricity companies in the UK.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: University/industry cooperation in transmission and distribution research
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Future for Research in Transmission and Distribution in the UK
abstract: There are at present about 18 departments in UK universities with some activity in power engineering of which a dozen or so have expertize in one or more aspects of research relevant to transmission and distribution plant and systems. The main concerns for the future are that there is adequate funding to maintain an effective research capability within the university system and that this capability is used to address those research issues which will be critical to the medium and long-term development of the electricity supply industry in the UK.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Distribution research requirements of a regional electricity company post privatisation
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Future for Research in Transmission and Distribution in the UK
abstract: While the fundamental need for research by regional electricity companies (RECs) has not changed since their formation, the climate and types of support for this research are now markedly different. Distribution research is now more strategically linked to the needs of RECs and this has already had some impact on the range of projects which are currently in progress. Research is now carried out in a wider range of organisations than before, each having its own particular range of skills and attractions which the new REC customer wants to buy.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Developments in the management of R&D in the National Grid Company
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Future for Research in Transmission and Distribution in the UK
abstract: As part of the break-up of the CEGB for privatisation, staff engaged in R&D in the transmission and system control areas were allocated to the new National Grid Company. The author highlights the principal developments which have taken place in the management of R&D in the National Grid Company. Company background; management principles; R&D planning; the 1992/93 R&D programme; and R&D collaboration are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Technical and organizational aspects of EPRI R&D
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Future for Research in Transmission and Distribution in the UK
abstract: This mission of the Electric Power Research Institute (EPRI) is to discover, develop and deliver advances in science and technology for the benefit of member utilities, their customers and society. Because of the breadth of its work EPRI has developed strategic relationships with other research and development organizations throughout the world. The author looks at planning and prioritization of R&D activities; transmission and distribution technologies; tailored collaboration and preparation for the future.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'The Future for Research in Transmission and Distribution in the UK' (Digest No.025)

articleTitle: University research-the profitable way forward (electrical engineering)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Future for Research in Transmission and Distribution in the UK
abstract: A scheme has been evolved which appears to bridge the academic and industrial divide. It provides industry with the advanced vision it requires to survive, with a price structure which it can accommodate. It provides university research groups with intellectually stimulating and relevant problems to solve which by virtue of their relevance attract income. Lastly, it provides young men and women with a unique vehicle upon which to develop there professional skills in an exciting and creative environment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
